title: United States sanctions Rosneft and Lukoil as Budapest summit is cancelled
body:
On Wednesday, 22 October 2025, the US Treasury announced sanctions on Rosneft and Lukoil, Russia's two largest oil companies. Novaya Gazeta estimated that together they account for almost half of Russia's crude oil exports. The measures were the first sanctions the Trump administration had imposed on Moscow since President Donald Trump returned to office in January 2025.

The Treasury said the sanctions were imposed because of Russia's "lack of serious commitment to a peace process" in Ukraine, and that they aimed to reduce the Kremlin's revenue for its war effort. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the measures responded to Vladimir Putin's "refusal to end this senseless war." He said further action was possible and urged allies to join the sanctions.

Trump called the sanctions "tremendous" and said he hoped they "won't be on for long." He also said he had cancelled the planned Budapest summit with Putin because it "didn't feel right," but that he still intended to meet Putin "in the future." Hungarian Foreign Minister Peter Szijjarto said Washington had not abandoned the idea of hosting the summit and that only the timing remained undecided.

On 23 October, European Union Vice President Kaja Kallas announced the EU's 19th sanctions package against Moscow. It targets Russian banks, crypto exchanges and entities in India and China, and restricts the movement of Russian diplomats.
